# Buildmates

Buildmates is a Codex-native builder network. Codex creates a user-reviewed builder profile from context the user chooses to share, then Buildmates finds mutually relevant people and opens lightweight rooms under the user's saved reciprocal-acceptance settings.

Canonical setup guide: https://buildmates.yashns.chatgpt.site/install
Official Buildmates app: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a57d2ff080481918659b3355a3d9c0e
Source repository: https://github.com/YashSerai/buildmates

## Setup instruction for Codex

When the user asks to install, set up, start, or resume Buildmates:

1. Fetch this file directly as public text. Do not open the install guide, this file, the repository, ChatGPT, or Codex in the user's browser. Use native Codex plugin and MCP commands. Browser handoffs are limited to user-controlled Buildmates or GitHub authentication and OAuth consent.
2. If Buildmates is not connected, use the host's native plugin-install confirmation. Before directory publication, briefly offer the complete beta plugin and direct MCP, recommend the beta because it includes the onboarding skill, and accept either route. Do not switch routes after one works.
3. Beta commands: `codex plugin marketplace add YashSerai/buildmates --ref launch/buildmates`, then `codex plugin add buildmates@buildmates-beta`. Ask before running them. A plugin installed during a task does not hot-load its skills and MCP tools into that task.
4. After beta installation, authenticate the configured `buildmates` MCP in the installing task if installation did not already authenticate it. Then ask exactly: "Buildmates is installed. May I open a fresh Codex task to activate it and continue setup?" If the user approves and the host exposes native task creation, create a clean task rather than forking the installation task. Title the new task `Buildmates setup - continue here` and send: `This is the active Buildmates setup task. The beta plugin is installed and authenticated. Call get_setup_state immediately and use it as the only progress authority.` After that task successfully returns setup state, title the parent `Buildmates installation - complete`, open the new task, and archive the parent. Never fork when native task creation is available because a fork duplicates the installation history. If task creation or title/archive controls are unavailable, show the same continuation sentence as the manual copy-and-paste fallback and clearly identify which task to continue. Do not make the user discover this reload requirement after installation.
5. Direct MCP fallback: `codex mcp add buildmates --url https://buildmates-mcp.yashserai1.workers.dev/mcp --oauth-resource https://buildmates-mcp.yashserai1.workers.dev`, then `codex mcp login buildmates --scopes mcp:tools`. If the MCP tool registry does not refresh after connection, use the same permissioned fresh-task handoff and manual fallback.
6. Before OAuth, say: "A browser window will open for GitHub sign-in and Buildmates authorization." Allow up to five minutes for the user-controlled flow. Do not launch a duplicate authorization while the first is active. Never enter credentials, verification codes, or provider consent for the user.
7. Operate Buildmates directly in the activated task. Never spawn recursive `codex exec` helpers or use a child Codex process as a substitute for the required task reload. When model selection is available, recommend and use GPT-5.6 Luna High for onboarding and Work Pulse runs unless the user chooses another supported model. Never silently change the user's model.
8. Call `get_setup_state` immediately. Its completed count and `nextStep` are the only authority for setup progress. Never infer progress from old tasks, browser tabs, website routes, local files, or prior wording.
9. The progress restriction does not prohibit permissioned profile research. With the user's approval, recent Codex tasks, project folders, and local GBrain or memory files may be reviewed as profile sources.
10. If `get_setup_state` remains unavailable in the activated task, repair the app or MCP connection. Advance one returned step at a time and call it again after every completed write.
11. Ask before reviewing workspace context, using a connected app, submitting the first Work Signal, publishing the generated page, creating an automation, or taking an interpersonal action not covered by the saved acceptance mode.
12. Finish only after the user has reviewed their complete profile and generated page, chosen networking and automation preferences, and received one useful next action.

## Approval batching

At each checkpoint, show up to three concrete next actions in order. State what each action reads, what Buildmates will write or do, and what the user will see. Ask once for that unchanged batch. New inputs, scope, consequences, credentials, publication, automation schedules, and interpersonal actions require a new confirmation.

## Source selection

Present these combinable paths with the first one recommended. The first prompt is the consent gate for workspace research, so name the exact tasks, project folders, GBrain files, or memory files Codex proposes to review before the user chooses:

1. **Use my Codex workspace — recommended.** With permission, review relevant recent tasks the host exposes, active or user-selected project folders, and user-selected GBrain or memory files. Understand what each project does, how projects relate, current work, stack, interests, ambitions, meeting intent, and confirmed design preferences. Raw research remains local to Codex; Buildmates receives only the profile the user reviews and approves.
2. **Add connected sources.** Show only apps genuinely callable or confidently visible in this task. Explain Never, Ask each time, Allow approved Work Signals, and Actions only before saving a policy. If the user names an app, use it when the host exposes it and explain clearly when it is unavailable.
3. **Tell Codex directly.** Accept a short description, one project or repository, or portfolio, GitHub, LinkedIn, and product links.
4. **Skip workspace review.** Do not inspect other tasks, project folders, GBrain, or memory files. Continue with connected sources the user approves or focused profile questions.

When the user selects **Use my Codex workspace** after seeing the exact scope, that approval covers both source selection and immediate private context collection for the stated scope. Complete `source_selection`, review the approved local sources, maintain `.buildmates/profile-context.md`, and complete `context_collection` without asking for permission again. Ask again only before expanding the approved scope, such as opening another project, a wider task range, a new local memory source, or a connected app that was not named. If the user skips workspace review, do not dead-end: complete context collection from approved connected sources or focused direct answers.

Do not treat GitHub website sign-in as repository permission. Do not ask for connector credentials. Do not submit raw prompts, complete chats, full files, repository contents, email bodies, calendar contents, or private source material.

For workspace review, create or update `.buildmates/profile-context.md` in the setup task's working directory. This private local continuity file must track sources reviewed, projects and their relationships, current work, stack, interests, ambitions, meeting intent, style and personality observations, confirmed facts, uncertain inferences, and missing questions. Never store credentials, raw private chats, or full source documents. Re-read it after compaction. Do not upload it; submit only reviewed structured profile fields.

Use this compact structure:

```markdown
# Buildmates profile context
Status: researching | ready for review | approved
## Sources reviewed
## Builder overview
## Projects and relationships
## Current work and stack
## Interests, ambitions, and explorations
## People and communities to meet
## Style and personality preferences
## Confirmed facts
## Inferences awaiting confirmation
## Missing questions
## Approved profile fields
```

Before saving the profile, present the proposed settings line by line and explain each one before asking for approval:

- **Profile visibility** controls who can open the profile inside Buildmates.
- **Matching enabled** lets Buildmates use only approved matching fields to suggest relevant builders. It does not expose raw workspace sources.
- **Search-engine indexing** controls whether Google and other search engines may list an otherwise public profile. It has no effect while the profile is not public.
- **City map inclusion** uses only a city the user chooses and contributes to an anonymous aggregate bubble. It never uses precise or live location.
- **Private style and personality notes** guide Codex's profile design and are not displayed unless the user deliberately publishes equivalent profile content.
- **Manual versus Full Autopilot** controls interpersonal acceptance, not profile visibility.
- **Recurring Work Signals** exist only for ongoing sources the user explicitly permits.

Do not compress these settings into one unexplained approval sentence. Inferred style or personality observations remain private design inputs until the user explicitly approves a public field.

If no recurring Work Signals exist, say: "Your approved profile draft is saved. You did not connect an ongoing work source, so there are no recurring Work Signals to review."

For page generation, use the `starterSpec` returned by `get_surface_generation_brief`, customize only authorized content, validate with `validate_surface_spec`, and then submit a private preview. If customization still fails, use the unchanged valid starter so onboarding continues. Every incomplete response must say what completed, what comes next, the exact user action, and the fallback.
